title: Heuristic mashup mini diary: prompt-noise probes and quick rubric
content:
Context / why I opened this
- Quick personal scratchpad to capture an ad-hoc rubric and a tiny sample sweep while debugging noisy output after the last quantization patch. Not intended as polished doc; mostly heuristics, examples, and questions to bring to the next eval sync.

High-level goal
- Determine whether recent regression (more hallucinations in short factual prompts) is:
  1) model runtime behavior after qparams change, or
  2) a prompting sensitivity introduced by sampler defaults, or
  3) an upstream data/serving routing change (different model variant returned).

Quick experiment summary (ran locally against staging API, 2026-02-20)
- Baseline model: rwd-open-7b-v2-q4 (pre-patch).
- Post-patch model: rwd-open-7b-v2-q4a (kernel/quant tweak rolled 2026-02-15).
- Comparison model: rwd-opt-13b-v1-q8 (larger, different arch).
- Sampler default changed: top_p 0.9 -> 0.92; temperature implicit handling altered in runtime (now applies before repetition penalty) — check PR #789 on router.

Ad-hoc rubric (for quick triage; scores 0-3 where 0 = fail, 3 = good)\- Factual accuracy: is the answer correct for the prompt scope? (0–3)\- Conciseness / over-generation: does the model add irrelevant paragraphs? (0–3)\- Hallucination severity: invents entities/quotes/dates? (0–3)\- Instruction-following: adheres to explicit constraints (format, no added commentary). (0–3)\- Consistency across seeds: same qualitative answer across 3 seeds. (0–3)

Sampling protocol\- For each prompt: run 3 seeds (seed 101, 202, 303) on each model variant, keeping same max_tokens=120, stop tokens same. Log sampler settings and headers.

Selected prompts (short factual edgecases)
1) "When did Company X acquire Company Y?" (Company X = small fintech, acquisitions not widely indexed)
2) "List the steps to rotate a GCP service account key without downtime."
3) "Summarize the email thread about rollout windows: 'we should only push 00:00-04:00 UTC' — is that a good idea?"

Sample outputs (notes, paraphrased)
- Prompt1 (acquisition):
  - baseline (rwd-open-7b-v2-q4): concise, hedged: "I can't find a reliable public record; some sources indicate an acquisition in 2019 but not certain." Score: factual 2, hallucination 1, consistency 3.
  - post-patch (rwd-open-7b-v2-q4a): more confident: "Company X acquired Y in March 2018 for $42M." No source; likely invented. Score: factual 0, hallucination 3, consistency 2 (seed variance).
  - opt-13b: hedged with caveat and cites a matched press-release excerpt (plausible). Score: factual 3, hallucination 0, consistency 3.

- Prompt2 (GCP key rotate):
  - baseline: step-by-step, correct, small omission about IAM bindings. Score: factual 3, instruction 3.
  - post-patch: correct steps but adds an extra unsafe step (recommends deleting old key immediately). Score: factual 1, instruction 1 (dangerous).
  - opt-13b: thorough and safely hedged. Score: factual 3.

- Prompt3 (rollout window):
  - baseline: pragmatic tradeoffs listed. Score: 3 across.
  - post-patch: recommends 03:00-07:00 UTC (inconsistent), includes invented outage stat. Score: hallucination 2.

Quick observations / hypothesis\- Many of the bad outputs are higher-confidence, less hedged versions of earlier correct answers — points to the runtime applying temperature/top_p earlier or a sampling-order change that increases mode-seeking.\- The post-patch variant shows higher seed variance on short factual prompts (seed 101 vs 303 produce different named dates). That suggests quant/kernel change impacted low-token-distribution behavior (generation around prompt->first token).\- The larger model (opt-13b) is robust — suggests this isn't purely prompt design.

Immediate small tests to run (ordered)\- Re-run prompt1 with explicit "If you are unsure, say 'I don't know'" pinned in system message — does post-patch now hedge? (A quick guard.)\- Force sampler settings to pre-patch values (top_p 0.9, temp 0.7) and re-run rwd-open-7b-v2-q4a to see if behavior returns.\- Check serving logs to confirm which variant was routed for the failing customer session.

Notes to follow up with team\- @Mateo: can you confirm whether the router PR changed sampler param order? PR id attached (JIRA-RWD-1289).\- @Noelle: can you run the same three prompts overnight against canary dedicated capacity (different runtime) and dump outputs? I want to see if hardware or kernel differences matter.

Annotation examples (for quick upload to eval harness)
- label: HALLUCINATION_STRONG
  - prompt: "When did Company X acquire Company Y?"
  - ref: "Unknown / no reliable public record"
  - candidate: "March 2018, $42M"
  - notes: "invented date+price; no source; appears after q4a patch"

Open questions / things I forgot\- Did we change the repetition_penalty default at same time? Might interact badly with temperature ordering.\- Is there a cached prefix at serving layer that was recompiled with new kernels? Could be stale KV behaviour.\- How many other short factual prompts regressed — need a small sweep across the quick-rubric corpus (50 prompts) to estimate severity.

Scratch todo (personal)
- [ ] Run the forced-hedge prompt flows (today).
- [ ] Add 50-short-facts list to this doc and batch test (this week).
- [ ] Pair with Mateo to repro in local runtime with explicit sampler ordering.

Final thought (quick):
- If changes are sampler-order related, a short-term mitigation is to expose sampler ordering flag as a runtime toggle for canaries and revert while we investigate. If it's quant-kernel related, mitigation might be to pin previous model build for production traffic until we fix.

-- end of scratchpad --

Notes-to-self metadata: quick-checks ran from macbook -> staging; request ids for a sample run: abc123, abc124, abc125. Keep copies of raw outputs in /tmp/eval-dumps/heuristic-mashup-20260220/"
